note: Detector definitions are DATA, not code. A snapshot records a fingerprint of this file, and `quality diff` refuses to compare across a fingerprint change, so adding a detector never reads as a regression. Same contract as session-reflection/patterns.json.

control.note: sloc is THE CONTROL SERIES, not a quality metric. Borg, Ezzouhri and Tornhill 2024 measured a naive LOC threshold at AUC 0.95, above every composite tested, so LOC is the bar a metric has to beat. `diff` prints its move beside every other move and flags any metric that merely tracked it.

banned.note: These are refused by construction, not merely unused. Each was rejected on evidence measured on this codebase; re-adding one needs a new measurement, not an opinion.

metrics.sum_ccn: r=0.910, R2=0.828 against per-file LOC here. Reported a false +6,198 regression on a refactor that improved the code.
metrics.maintainability_index: r(MI, ln SLOC) = -0.876 on Python here, -0.787 across 369 files in ~/code. Its -16.2*ln(sloc) term pays you to split files.
metrics.sqale_debt_ratio: Borg et al. 2024: AUC 0.60 against a 0.50 coin flip, SonarQube's shipped default below the ROC diagonal. Its denominator means deleting lines raises the ratio.
metrics.halstead: Hamer and Frewin 1982 found the underpinning relationships are neither natural laws nor useful engineering approximations.
metrics.test_to_prod_ratio: LOC divided by LOC. Moved 9% here on a file-selection decision before any code changed.

detectors.summary: files that change together but reference each other in no way a tool can follow
detectors.why: The strongest result in the 2026-09-06 research. Found byte-identical sw.js copies, and a TypeScript-to-Go telemetry contract whose only link is a comment, which is why five events silently drifted. No type checker, linter or dependency graph can see either.
detectors.regression: a new pair above min_degree, or any pair reaching 1.0 (that is a duplicated file)

detectors.summary: share of the window's file-touches landing in the top 10 files
detectors.why: Rahman and Devanbu 2013 under effort-aware evaluation. Rising concentration means work piling into the same places.
detectors.regression: a rise of more than 5 points over two consecutive runs while sloc holds steady

detectors.summary: files with 5 or more fix commits in the defect window
detectors.why: Defect history is the least gameable signal available, and it needs no tool beyond git.

detectors.summary: percent of commits that revert or immediately re-fix a commit less than 24h old
detectors.why: An outcome, not a proxy. Cannot be improved by rewriting a function.
detectors.regression: a rise of more than 5 points over two consecutive runs while the commit count holds steady

detectors.summary: does the test suite pass, and does it terminate
detectors.why: A red or hanging suite makes every other number in the snapshot unreadable, so it gates first.

detectors.summary: imports crossing a declared architectural boundary
detectors.why: Found the known store-to-components inversion plus two the audit missed, in under ten seconds. Deterministic and fixed by one import.
detectors.regression: any increase at an unchanged config fingerprint

detectors.summary: percent of lines inside a detected clone
detectors.why: Recorded, NEVER gated. Rahman, Bird and Devanbu found cloned code less defect-prone than non-cloned code, and the number falls when you add unduplicated code. It moved 0.13 to 0.13 across a refactor that removed real duplication.
detectors.regression: none, this series is context for reading the others
